title: The Quiet Language
premise: Dominic Voss, a literary translator in his forties, has spent fifteen years in a city far from home, translating other people's words while letting his mother tongue—Kavreni, a language spoken only inside his family's house—erode word by borrowed word. When the childhood home is put up for auction after his father's death, Dominic returns to help his siblings sort the estate and discovers a locked drawer of his grandmother's letters written entirely in Kavreni, letters that reveal why the family stopped speaking it aloud. As the auction date closes in, old silences between Dominic, his brother Tomas, and sister Marta fracture into open reckoning over what each of them gave up to survive their father's household. In the end, Dominic chooses not to bid on the house but to read one letter aloud at the sale—translating Kavreni into the language he hid behind—and walks away owning nothing except the language itself, which he begins, haltingly, to speak again.
about_author: Elodie Nakamura is a former court interpreter who grew up between three languages and two continents, and whose fiction examines what families say by refusing to speak. She lives in Rotterdam, where she teaches translation workshops for writers working across inherited tongues.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Word
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In Rotterdam, Dominic finishes translating a novel whose author thanks him for 'preserving her voice,' a phrase that stings. He reaches for a Kavreni word for grief and finds only its Dutch substitute waiting. Emotional beat: quiet self-estrangement; the erosion has become ordinary.

chapters.title: Notice of Sale
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A letter from a probate solicitor announces the auction of the family house on Vossstraat. He drafts three replies to his siblings and sends none. Emotional beat: dread disguised as administrative calm; the past acquires a deadline.

chapters.title: Marta Counts the Rooms
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. In the emptying house, Marta inventories furniture with an auctioneer's efficiency, refusing to enter the upstairs study. She catalogs objects precisely because she cannot catalog feelings. Emotional beat: controlled grief, resentment at being the one who stayed nearby all these years.

chapters.title: Tomas Comes Back Early
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas arrives from abroad weeks before anyone expected, cheerful and armed with jokes, already negotiating with a developer friend about the property. His breeziness is armor. Emotional beat: performance of moving on; the reader sees the cost beneath it.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Walking the house alone at night, Dominic finds the rooms still organized around his father's chair, his mother's silence, the kitchen where Kavreni was spoken and nowhere else. Emotional beat: the body remembering a language the mind has let go.

chapters.title: The Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Clearing the study, Marta forces the locked desk drawer and finds bundles of letters in Kavreni, written by their grandmother Ana over thirty years. She photographs them instead of reading them and says nothing to her brothers. Emotional beat: temptation and secrecy; inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Almost Saying It
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At dinner with his siblings, conversation slides around the letters, the language, the father—the art of almost saying it, practiced by everyone at once. Tomas proposes selling fast; Marta agrees too quickly. Emotional beat: complicity of silence reasserting itself.

chapters.title: Ana's Hand
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Unable to sleep, Dominic takes one letter and reads slowly, translating in the margins like a student. The first letter describes Ana arriving in the country, deciding the family would keep Kavreni indoors 'so it could not be taken.' Emotional beat: wonder and vertigo; the language comes back faster than expected.

chapters.title: The Rule of Indoors
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas remembers childhood: Kavreni as the secret language of punishment and comfort both, the way their father used it to exclude, their mother to console. He wants the letters burned. Emotional beat: anger surfacing through nostalgia; the language was never neutral.

chapters.title: Appraisal
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The auctioneer values the house and its contents; a stranger prices the kitchen table where every important sentence of Dominic's childhood was spoken. Marta watches him measure rooms and feels unseen grief turn to resolve. Emotional beat: commodification clarifying what cannot be sold.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Flashback chapter: how Dominic left at twenty-three, took translation work, and let Kavreni slip—one word replaced per year—as a deliberate survival strategy after a final fight with his father. Emotional beat: compassion for his younger self; understanding that forgetting was a choice made under pressure.

chapters.title: The Letter That Names It
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Deep in Ana's correspondence, Dominic finds the letter the whole family arranged itself around: Ana writing of a betrayal during the war years, a neighbor denounced because of the family's foreign speech, and the vow of indoor silence that followed. Emotional beat: the origin of everything revealed; fear dressed up as tradition.

chapters.title: Marta Reads One Too
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta finally reads the photographed letters herself and realizes Dominic has been ahead of her. Confrontation in the kitchen—not about the house but about who gets to interpret the family. Emotional beat: rivalry transmuted into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Tomas's Offer
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas secures a private buyer offering above asking price, contingent on quick closure, and asks his siblings to waive the auction. He frames it as mercy; it is also control. Emotional beat: the family's oldest dynamic—buying peace—repeating itself.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. With days left, Dominic must decide whether to contest the private sale or let the house go silently, as the family always did. He translates another letter and finds Ana, near the end of her life, regretting the vow: 'We saved the language and lost each other.' Emotional beat: rising tension; the question becomes unavoidable.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: All three siblings, alternating short passages. At the kitchen table, Dominic finally asks it aloud: what did each of us give up to survive this house, and was it worth it? The dinner detonates—old accusations, the father's cruelty, the mother's complicity, Tomas's exile, Marta's staying. Emotional beat: climax of rupture; the arranged silence collapses.

chapters.title: Night Before the Sale
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. After the fight, the siblings separately wander the dark house. Marta finds Tomas sitting in the father's study, not angry, just small. They speak plainly for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: exhaustion after rupture; the first honest tenderness.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The auction room: strangers bidding on the family's life in increments. Tomas's private deal dissolves when the buyer withdraws; the gavel falls to an outside bidder anyway. Emotional beat: anticlimax as truth—the house was never going to be kept.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the empty porch after the sale, Dominic reads Ana's key letter aloud, first in Kavreni, then translating line by line into the shared language, with Marta and Tomas listening. Emotional beat: catharsis; the indoor language spoken outdoors at last, grief given grammar.

chapters.title: Division of Remains
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The siblings divide what's left: Marta takes the kitchen table, Tomas takes almost nothing but asks for one letter, Dominic takes the bundle. They agree, without ceremony, to meet once a year. Emotional beat: settlement without erasure; inheritance redistributed as meaning rather than property.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Back in Rotterdam, Dominic begins teaching himself the Kavreni he lost, using Ana's letters as primer, making errors, keeping a notebook of recovered words. He writes to his siblings in it, badly, knowing they'll understand. Emotional beat: tentative renewal; belonging rebuilt from fragments.

chapters.title: The Quiet Language
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing. A year later, standing outside the sold house now owned by strangers, Dominic speaks a full Kavreni sentence to the empty street—naming his father, forgiving no one and everyone—and walks to the station where Marta waits. Emotional beat: resolution; the price of survival acknowledged, the language carried forward out loud.
